title: Juniper and the Trail
premise: Cyrus Nystrom, estranged son of legendary archaeologist Dr. Ingrid Nystrom and the best trail-finder her expeditions ever produced, has spent five years guiding survey crews through remote wilderness to avoid the family name. When his father's old rival, Marcus Vale, hires the crew for a dig at the forbidden source of the Kestrel River — a site Ingrid swore off after a disaster that killed Cyrus's brother — Cyrus is pulled in against his will. Racing the brief window before glacier calving season seals the route, he discovers the 'treasure' is evidence that Vale's mentor looted and falsified the original discovery, a truth Ingrid buried to protect the living. Cyrus must choose between exposing the truth and protecting his father's legacy; in the end he follows the river to its source, finds both the proof and his father waiting there, and they choose justice over reputation together, publishing the truth as partners rather than rivals' pawns.
about_author: Orsen Ishikawa is a former river guide who spent a decade leading expeditions through glacial valleys before turning to fiction full-time. Their novels are known for terrain so vivid readers check their boots for mud.

chapters.title: Miles, Not Years
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. On a routine survey contract in the northern ranges, Cyrus measures his life in trail miles, dodging calls from his father and keeping his famous surname quiet. When the crew's new client is revealed as Marcus Vale — Ingrid's oldest rival — and the job is the Kestrel Source dig, Cyrus's stomach drops. Emotional beat: the past arriving like weather you can't outrun.

chapters.title: The Contract with Teeth
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. Vale offers triple pay and a clause binding the crew to secrecy about the site's history. The crew's leader, Rhea, needs the money; Cyrus nearly walks, until he learns Vale already sent an advance team upriver without permits. Guilt and duty tangle: if someone dies on that route because he said no, it's on him. Emotional beat: reluctant commitment.

chapters.title: What Ingrid Swore Off
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Cyrus and flashback chapters from Ingrid's expedition journal, twenty years earlier. We learn the first Kestrel expedition ended in a crevasse collapse that killed Cyrus's older brother Anders — and that Ingrid sealed the valley's location and forbade all return. Cyrus rereads the journal he stole from her office years ago. Emotional beat: grief re-opened like a wound in thawing ground.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The crew pushes up the Kestrel gorge, racing the calving season. Cyrus proves why he's the better digger, reading water and scree where Vale's maps fail, earning the crew's trust while quietly planning to sabotage anything that endangers them. He notices Vale's advance team left markers — fresh ones, wrong ones. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: The Woman at the Ford
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. At a high ford the crew meets Sela Vann, a park warden working the valley off-book, investigating illegal salvage in protected land. She should arrest them; instead she trades information — she's been tracking Vale for two years. Sparks fly between her and Cyrus even as she makes clear she'll do her duty no matter what grows between them. Emotional beat: love meeting duty head-on.

chapters.title: Calving Season Opens Early
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus and Sela. A warm front collapses the schedule: the glacier begins calving days ahead of forecast, and the route's ice bridge will close within the week. One crew member, Tomas, is injured in a rockfall caused by Vale cutting corners. Cyrus realizes Vale knew the risks and hid them. Emotional beat: the mountain stops being scenery and becomes an adversary.

chapters.title: The False Ledger
chapters.summary: POV: Sela. At the advance camp, Sela and Cyrus find Vale's real objective: not artifacts but the field ledger proving his late mentor, Halloran, looted the source site and forged its provenance — the fraud Ingrid discovered and buried. Vale intends to destroy the ledger and pin the old crime on Ingrid. Emotional beat: the revelation that reframes everything.

chapters.title: The Ice Bridge
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. With hours before the bridge fails, Vale takes the ledger and pushes for the source alone; Cyrus goes after him across the failing ice, saving him when it calves beneath them. Stranded together on the far side, Vale confesses the depth of his obsession — Halloran was his father figure, and the truth would unmake him. Emotional beat: hatred cracking into something almost like pity.

chapters.title: The Source
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. At the forbidden spring beneath the glacier, Cyrus finds the original cache — and Ingrid herself, who came ahead of everyone, unable to stay away from her sons' grave-country. Mother and son confront twenty years of silence, Anders's death, and her choice to bury the truth. They retrieve the ledger together as the glacier groans. Emotional beat: reconciliation bought with honesty, not comfort.

chapters.title: Downriver
chapters.summary: POV: Cyrus. The crew descends by the emergency route Sela mapped; Vale, broken by the confession he can no longer bury, turns state's evidence. Sela files her report knowing it implicates people she cares about — justice outside convenience. Cyrus publishes the corrected record under his own name at last, standing beside his mother. Emotional beat: belonging found not in escaping the past but in carrying it well.
